Change mid-process exit to return

If the user wanted to exit in the middle of, say, adding a book or searching for existing books, it was done by throwing and catching an exception.  I realized that’s a pretty weird way of doing it, so I switched to returning values instead.  Makes more sense.

Also it’s not stated in the UX, but if either the search field or search terms are blank (in searching for local books), it will gently return you to the main screen.

Unicode Support Proper

Pyberry now supports Unicode in any of the fields that accept string data.  It uses unicodedata's normalize function to normalize it to ascii, instead of just dropping any unicode characters or misrepresenting them.  So, a string like 'Løng' would become 'Long'.

Backport to Python 2.7

This is a major release, as I've decided to move to Python 2.7 (from Python 3) due to module reasons.  This commit sees all of the code transformed into Python 2.x syntax.

Additionally, due to the change, I could fix several outstanding issues.  This fixes #2 because the whole lookup class is rewritten to use the Google API library module.  Although I only added search by title, it should be very straightforward to be add any other attribute, so this closes #3.

It also fixes #10, although that doesn't mean that multiple authors are completely supported, only that there's the option in the future.

Fix searching

Fix searching of database.  It's not done in a "proper" way, but it uses string formatting for the search field but as a caution it checks possible fields against a list of valid ones.

I feel this is a reasonable approach because it simply will not work any other way.  Due to the design of the pysqlite3 module, placeholders cannot be used for the column names.  Because I was able to mitigate the chances of a SQL injection attack by checking any input against a list of valid ones it should remain secure.
